problem: Existing visual navigation methods (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, sim-trained point-goal agents) are trained on suburban/indoor/static data and fail in dynamic, map-free urban settings needing common-sense rules (crossings, sidewalks, crowds); teleoperation data is too small and diverse-lacking, and VLM-prompted action labeling is costly and hard to scale.
motivation: Urban last-mile delivery robots need human-like navigation between GPS waypoints, but urban norms are hard to simulate and hard to collect via teleoperation. Abundant web city-walking/driving videos capture these behaviors, and noisy visual-odometry pseudo-labels over short windows are sufficient action supervision for scalable imitation learning.
key_idea: Train a transformer navigation policy by imitation on 2000+ hours of YouTube walking and driving videos with action labels from off-the-shelf visual odometry (DPVO), then fine-tune on a small amount of teleoperated expert data.
insight: Scale of noisy, VO-labeled web video matters: zero-shot performance improves with data size, and beyond ~1000 hours it beats fine-tuned ViNT (Fig. 6); mixing driving and walking gives 250 hours matching 1000 hours of walking alone, indicating cross-domain/embodiment transfer. Ablations (Tab. 3) show fine-tuning is the main gain (17.03→15.23 MAOE), while orientation loss and feature hallucination give only marginal gains within noise; feature hallucination hurts zero-shot but helps after fine-tuning.
method: Video data + VO labels: ~2000 h of YouTube city-walking (and driving) videos; DPVO gives relative poses used only within short windows (5 past, 5 future) to avoid drift.

Scale normalization: each action is normalized by the average step length in its trajectory to resolve VO scale ambiguity and embodiment differences; denormalized with the robot's step length at deployment.

Architecture: frozen DINOv2 ViT-B/14 encodes 5 past frames; polar/Fourier coordinate MLP encodes 5 past positions plus target waypoint; a 16-layer transformer decodes to an action head (5 future waypoints) and an arrival head.
Feature hallucination: auxiliary MSE loss aligning output tokens with DINOv2 features of future frames (training only).
Losses: L1 action + negative cosine orientation loss + BCE arrival + feature loss (weights 1, 5, 1, 0.1).
Fine-tuning: 6 h of teleoperated quadruped data in NYC (Unitree Go1, LiDAR-SLAM ground-truth poses); 9 h held out for offline test.
Evaluation metrics: average/maximum orientation error (AOE/MAOE) per critical scenario (turn, crossing, detour, proximity, crowd) plus L2 and arrival accuracy.

setting.backbone: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 (frozen) + 16-layer transformer policy (trained from scratch, 214M total/127M trainable)
setting.training_data: ~2000 h YouTube city-walking videos (plus driving videos in ablation) with DPVO pseudo-labels; fine-tuned on 6 h teleoperation data collected in NYC
setting.observation: monocular RGB (5 past frames), past positions, and target GPS waypoint
setting.action_space: 5 predicted future relative waypoints (2D, normalized step-length) plus arrival flag; executed by PD controller as velocity commands
setting.simulator: real world only (offline evaluation on teleop data + real-world deployment)
setting.privileged: none (GPS from a phone used for position; GT LiDAR-SLAM poses only for training/offline eval labels)

numbers.eval_set_note: 9 h held-out teleoperation data in NYC
numbers.backbone: DINOv2 + transformer, 2000 h videos + 6 h expert fine-tuning

numbers.eval_set_note: 9 h held-out teleoperation data in NYC
8-14 real-world trials per case (forward/left/right), targets 50-100 m away, Unitree Go1 in NYC
numbers.extra: success = predicts arrival within 5 m; human interruption counts as failure

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; results are on the authors' own offline NYC teleop test set and real-world trials. Offline table values given as scenario means; per-scenario values also in Table 1.
results: Fine-tuned CityWalker achieves real-world success 77.3% vs 57.1% for fine-tuned ViNT and 42.9% for zero-shot NoMaD, and best offline MAOE/arrival in most scenarios (mean MAOE 15.2° vs 16.5° ViNT fine-tuned). The zero-shot model matches or beats fine-tuned baselines on arrival, and zero-shot performance scales with data.
limitations: Sensitive to noisy phone GPS location readings in deployment
Weaker in detour scenarios and Turn after fine-tuning (data proportion mismatch); small offline test set makes ablation gains within noise
Slow inference with DINOv2 (1.7 fps on RTX 3060) unless swapped for a lighter backbone; real-world trial counts are small
